To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) Brain spectrin 235/240 and 235/240E are differentially expressed in dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons during early chicken DRG development in vivo and during DRG development in culture.
brain spectrin isoform 240/235 was expressed transiently in the ventrolateral neurons and exhibited a somato –axonal distribution pattern.

brain spectrin isoform 240/235, a membrane-related cytoskeletal protein is preferentially located in the perikarya and axons of dorsal root ganglion neurons, whereas brain spectrin 235/240E is restricted to the soma of a selected population of neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression, localization and function of brain spectrin isoform in the nervous system.
the role of the cytoskeleton in the differentiation and maturation processes of sensory neurons.
the role of spectrin in the development and function of neuronal cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

brain spectrin isoform expression in sensory neurons is developmentally regulated, that brain spectrin is differentially expressed in different neuronal cell populations and that it is differentially distributed within a single neuron.
brain spectrin expression is a dynamic process and is differentially regulated in the neuronal cell body and in axons.
the two brain spectrin isoform types are not only differentially expressed in the developing dorsal root ganglion but are also differentially localized within neuronal cell bodies and processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
brain spectrin isoform 240/235 seems to be associated with axons and brain spectrin isoforme 240/235 E seems to be associated only with the soma.
the two isoforms of brain spectrin are differentially expressed during the early development of dorsal root ganglia.
brain spectrin isoform 240/235 seems to be involved in the axonal development, whereas isoform 240235E is involved in the maintenance of the neuronal cell body.
The main takeaway from our work is that
brain spectrin is a good marker for the study of the differentiation of dorsal root ganglion cells.
spectrin isoform expression and localization is differentially regulated in the developing nervous system.
the brain spectrin isoform 240/235 seems to be involved in the axonal processes and 240/ 235E is involved in the stabilization and cytoarchitecture of the soma.
